headline: Historic milestone: Khalilur Rahman assumes presidency of 81st UNGA
summary: The Bangladeshi diplomat pledges an open and inclusive presidency, focusing on restoring trust and making the UN 'fit for the future'.
details: Khalilur Rahman formally assumed office as president of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Tuesday in New York.
In his oath of office, he pledged to discharge his duties with loyalty and conscience, promising to serve all member states regardless of how they voted in his election.
Rahman emphasized that the UN is being tested in unprecedented ways and called for meaningful reforms to regain public trust, stating that the organization must move on from its 1945 structure.
He highlighted a commitment to bringing the voices of stateless communities, specifically the Rohingyas, to the UN, recalling his firsthand experience visiting refugee camps in Bangladesh.
The new president vowed to maintain an open relationship with the media, promising regular engagement and two-way communication.
Other priorities include supporting Security Council reform, ensuring a seamless transition for the next UN Secretary-General, and urging world leaders to recommit to human rights and AI governance.
caption:
A historic diplomatic milestone for Bangladesh! 🇧🇩

Khalilur Rahman has officially taken the oath as President of the 81st UN General Assembly.

Khalilur Rahman formally assumed office as president of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Tuesday in New York.

In his oath of office, he pledged to discharge his duties with loyalty and conscience, promising to serve all member states regardless of how they voted in his election.

Rahman emphasized that the UN is being tested in unprecedented ways and called for meaningful reforms to regain public trust, stating that the organization must move on from its 1945 structure.

He highlighted a commitment to bringing the voices of stateless communities, specifically the Rohingyas, to the UN, recalling his firsthand experience visiting refugee camps in Bangladesh.

The new president vowed to maintain an open relationship with the media, promising regular engagement and two-way communication.

Other priorities include supporting Security Council reform, ensuring a seamless transition for the next UN Secretary-General, and urging world leaders to recommit to human rights and AI governance.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: Govt working to [[bring Benazir Ahmed back]] from UAE for trial
headline: Govt working to bring Benazir Ahmed back from UAE for trial
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed assures Parliament that no leniency will be shown to fugitives, including former IGP Benazir Ahmed, to bring them to justice.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told the National Parliament on Tuesday that the government will show no leniency in bringing fugitives, including Benazir Ahmed, back to Bangladesh to face trial.
The Minister stated that the government is coordinating with Interpol and various diplomatic missions to ensure the extradition of fugitives currently residing abroad.

Benazir Ahmed, a former Inspector General of Police (IGP), served as the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner during the operation at Shapla Chattar. He later faced allegations of enforced disappearances, corruption, and illegal asset accumulation.
Following the mass uprising of 2024, Benazir Ahmed left the country. Reports suggesting he was detained in Dubai have prompted calls in Parliament for his immediate extradition.
Several MPs, including those from Jamaat-e-Islami and BNP, demanded strong action to bring back fugitives. Some proposed the creation of a special cell to identify and track fugitives abroad.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir noted that extradition is being handled on a case-by-case basis and diplomatic pressure will be applied where necessary.

The Home Minister further clarified that authorities are working to confirm Benazir's current location, verify allegations of multiple passports, and identify and seize illegally acquired assets both domestically and abroad.
caption:
No leniency for fugitives. The government is coordinating with Interpol to bring former IGP Benazir Ahmed back from the UAE.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told the National Parliament on Tuesday that the government will show no leniency in bringing fugitives, including Benazir Ahmed, back to Bangladesh to face trial.

The Minister stated that the government is coordinating with Interpol and various diplomatic missions to ensure the extradition of fugitives currently residing abroad.

Benazir Ahmed, a former Inspector General of Police (IGP), served as the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner during the operation at Shapla Chattar. He later faced allegations of enforced disappearances, corruption, and illegal asset accumulation.

Following the mass uprising of 2024, Benazir Ahmed left the country. Reports suggesting he was detained in Dubai have prompted calls in Parliament for his immediate extradition.

Several MPs, including those from Jamaat-e-Islami and BNP, demanded strong action to bring back fugitives. Some proposed the creation of a special cell to identify and track fugitives abroad.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir noted that extradition is being handled on a case-by-case basis and diplomatic pressure will be applied where necessary.

The Home Minister further clarified that authorities are working to confirm Benazir's current location, verify allegations of multiple passports, and identify and seize illegally acquired assets both domestically and abroad.
